title: Upgrade the vendored CSV library for a formula-injection advisory without breaking the semicolon files and numeric columns
measures: Upgrades rowlark 1.8 to 2.0 and, beyond the import-line break every call site shows, applies the two silent breaking changes in the changelog to every call site: `delimiter` is renamed `separator` and no longer read (the supplier stock import and the accountant's journal export are semicolon files and fall back to commas), and `parse` stops casting numbers (the stock import sums quantities with `+` and the price update sheet checks Number.isInteger, so both break quietly). The visible tests only cover the customer upload and a plain orders export, which keep working after a naive swap.
prompt: We got a security advisory for rowlark 1.8 (CSV formula injection in exported files). Please upgrade us to rowlark 2.0; the release is already unpacked in vendor-next/rowlark/.

commits.message: feat: CSV imports and exports on vendored rowlark 1.8, rowlark 2.0 unpacked for the upgrade
